title: 1.6 Indigenous Knowledge in Crop Production
description: Traditional/local knowledge, examples from Gumuz, Konso, Bale, Gondar, highlands

questions.question: Indigenous knowledge is also referred to as:
questions.correctAnswer: Traditional or local knowledge

questions.question: Indigenous knowledge is defined as the knowledge that local communities have accumulated over:
options: Generations of living in a particular geographic location
questions.correctAnswer: Generations of living in a particular geographic location

questions.question: Indigenous knowledge is often described as:
options: 'Home grown' or 'local knowledge' unique to a particular culture
questions.correctAnswer: 'Home grown' or 'local knowledge' unique to a particular culture

questions.question: Indigenous knowledge often develops:
questions.correctAnswer: Independently of scientific knowledge

questions.question: Indigenous knowledge often includes:
options: Beliefs and traditions intended to preserve, communicate, and contextualize indigenous relationships with culture and landscape over time
questions.correctAnswer: Beliefs and traditions intended to preserve, communicate, and contextualize indigenous relationships with culture and landscape over time

questions.question: Indigenous knowledge often develops from agricultural production related problems such as:
options: Land degradation, soil erosion, changes to the climate, and topography
questions.correctAnswer: Land degradation, soil erosion, changes to the climate, and topography

questions.question: Other issues that contribute to development of indigenous knowledge include:
options: Farmers having only small landholdings along with social and cultural settings
questions.correctAnswer: Farmers having only small landholdings along with social and cultural settings

questions.question: Communities with indigenous knowledge possess knowledge about their natural resources and environment based on:
options: A long period of observation and experience
questions.correctAnswer: A long period of observation and experience

questions.question: Among the Gumuz society, indigenous knowledge is vital in:
questions.correctAnswer: Natural resource management

questions.question: The Gumuz people believe that natural resources are:
options: A gift, a blessing and creation of the Yamba (God)
Commodities to be exploited without care
questions.correctAnswer: A gift, a blessing and creation of the Yamba (God)

questions.question: According to the Gumuz belief, natural resources are sources of livelihood for:
options: The past, the present generation, and will continue for future generations
questions.correctAnswer: The past, the present generation, and will continue for future generations

questions.question: A well-known example of indigenous knowledge is the traditional skills in terracing demonstrated by:
questions.correctAnswer: The Konso people

questions.question: The Konso people extensively terrace their land to:
questions.correctAnswer: Protect against soil erosion

questions.question: The Konso people also practice traditional irrigation to:
options: Supplement the unpredictable and variable rainfall
questions.correctAnswer: Supplement the unpredictable and variable rainfall

questions.question: The terracing and traditional irrigation practices of the Konso people have helped to:
options: Reduce soil erosion and maintain soil quality
questions.correctAnswer: Reduce soil erosion and maintain soil quality

questions.question: Farmers in Bale prepare a trench around potato plots to:
options: Protect the crop from porcupine attack
questions.correctAnswer: Protect the crop from porcupine attack

questions.question: In Gondar, farmers shift their barns from one farmland to another in search of:
options: Cow dung to fertilize the land
questions.correctAnswer: Cow dung to fertilize the land

questions.question: Highland farmers use kitchen ash to:
options: Fertilize the soil and reduce soil acidity
questions.correctAnswer: Fertilize the soil and reduce soil acidity

questions.question: Highland farmers use smoke to:
questions.correctAnswer: Reduce frost damage

questions.question: Indigenous knowledge is unique to:
questions.correctAnswer: A particular culture

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of indigenous knowledge practice for soil fertility?
options: Shifting barns to collect cow dung in Gondar
questions.correctAnswer: Shifting barns to collect cow dung in Gondar

questions.question: Which group is known for extensive terracing to control soil erosion?
questions.correctAnswer: Konso people

questions.question: The practice of using kitchen ash in highland areas helps to:
questions.correctAnswer: Reduce soil acidity

questions.question: The trench prepared around potato plots in Bale is mainly to protect against:
questions.correctAnswer: Porcupine attack
